h1: Boerne, TX land clearing for acreage home sites
lede: 9 Arrow Land Service handles land clearing in Boerne, TX for acreage home sites, from the first driveway cut to the building pad. Boerne is west of Bulverde on SH 46, out from our Spring Branch base.

answer.q: What does land clearing in Boerne, TX include for a new home site?
answer.a: Land clearing in Boerne, TX for a new home site usually includes a driveway route, a cleared building area, roots grubbed where the slab goes, and a graded pad. 9 Arrow Land Service handles that sequence with mulchers, dozers and excavators, keeping the live oaks you want and grinding the rest in place.

highlights: On-site rock crushed into road base
Selective clearing keeps the trees you want
Excavation up to about 4 feet deep

sections.h2: Boerne property along I-10 and Cibolo Creek
paras: Boerne is the Kendall County seat, northwest of San Antonio where I-10 and US 87 run past town. Cibolo Creek flows through Boerne. SH 46 crosses town and heads east toward Bulverde, and the interstate runs northwest through Comfort.

Boerne land splits three ways. In-town lots with neighbors close by. Acreage home sites in the hills outside town. Ranch tracts farther out with long fence lines and more cedar than grass. Each one needs a different mix of clearing and dirt work.

The ground under Boerne is limestone, and the area is known for its caves, with Cascade Caverns southeast of town and Cave Without a Name to the northeast. For a Boerne home site, that usually means rock close to the surface, live oak and Ashe juniper on top, and dirt work planned around what the excavator finds.

sections.h2: How Boerne home site land clearing comes together
paras: Home site land clearing in Boerne works best in order. Route the driveway first so trucks can reach the build. Clear the building area selectively, keeping the trees that make the lot worth buying. Grub roots only where the foundation goes. Then cut and fine-grade the pad.

[Land clearing for a building site](site-prep) and [site work and utility installation](site-work-light-utility-installation) cover that whole run on a Boerne lot, including excavation for septic systems and propane tanks and trenching for waterlines 3 inches or smaller. We work alongside your builder, engineer and licensed trades, who make the final connections.

Plenty of Boerne acreage has loose limestone on top. On-site rock crushing breaks that surface rock down into fine, compactible road base, which eliminates imported material, reduces project cost and speeds completion.

[Access road building](roads-and-access-preparation) on a Boerne property adds grading with a proper crown, drainage and culverts where water crosses, so the drive carries heavy equipment and truck traffic and stays usable through changing weather.

process.detail: Clear and rough-grade the access so equipment and trucks can reach the build.
Selectively mulch cedar and brush, keeping the live oaks you want to save.
Remove roots under the future foundation, then mulch the root balls on site.
Cut and fine-grade the pad, then trench for small waterlines, conduit and septic lines.
Crush surface rock into road base and finish the drive with a proper crown.

faqs.q: Can you clear a Boerne lot with HOA or deed restrictions?
faqs.a: Yes. Selective clearing lets a Boerne owner take out cedar and brush while keeping the trees an HOA or deed restriction protects. Share the restrictions and your site plan during the discovery call, and we plan the clearing around what has to stay before a machine starts on the lot.

faqs.q: What drives the cost of clearing a Boerne home site?
faqs.a: The cost of clearing a Boerne home site depends on tree density, tree size and species, slope, soil, and how easily machines reach and move around the site. A grassy pad near the road and a wooded hillside lot price very differently. Estimates come by the day or by the acre after a site visit.

faqs.q: Can you dig for a septic system on a rocky Boerne lot?
faqs.a: Yes. 9 Arrow excavates for septic systems and propane tanks on rocky Boerne lots, using dozers and excavation equipment built for rocky terrain and difficult soil, with excavation up to about 4 feet deep. We coordinate with your licensed trades and engineer on the rest of the system.
